samples.summary: Second copy of the sheet-comment CRDT helpers: `toYorkieMs`/`fromYorkieMs`/`copyThread`/`applyAddThread`/`applyAddReply`/`applyEditComment`/`applyDeleteComment` are re-implemented here, while `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts` already implements the same functions over the same stored shape. This PR deliberately hoisted mentions and notification planning into `@wafflebase/sheets` so the editor and the API could not disagree, but left these two writers of the identical `sheets[tabId].comments` shape separate — and they have already diverged (see the `delete` guard finding). Both work today; the risk is drift, since a future change to the Long boundary or the delete-root-comment rule has to land in two places.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:12-18 (`toYorkieMs`/`fromYorkieMs`), :42-58 (`copyThread`), :71-126 (`applyAddThread`/`applyAddReply`/`applyEditComment`/`applyDeleteComment`) — the pre-existing implementation the new `comment-ops.ts` duplicates rather than reuses.

samples.summary: `initialBoardRoot()` is duplicated. The backend's new copy seeds `{ meta: { title: 'Untitled board' }, elements: [] }`, which is byte-identical to the frontend's today, so nothing breaks — but the Yorkie SDK writes every absent `initialRoot` key on *each* attach, so the two seeds are contributing keys to the same document. If either side gains a field (a default `unit`, a viewport), the other keeps seeding the old shape and whoever attaches first decides what the document has.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/types/board-document.ts:8-10 — `initialBoardRoot()` for the same board Yorkie root, consumed by `boardInitialRootForRole` (:26) and `apply-imported-content.ts:228`.

samples.summary: The contract the new `applySetResolved` documents — Yorkie's object proxy routes `delete` to `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey`, which throws `fail to find <key>` for a key that was never set — is violated at the editor's own sheet-comment site, which deletes `resolvedAt`/`resolvedBy` unguarded when reopening. Pre-existing code, not introduced here, and only reachable if an unresolve runs against a thread with no `resolvedAt` (e.g. a thread the API set `resolved:false` on, or one resolved by a peer whose fields were never synced), which is why the editor's usual path is safe. Flagged because this PR is what establishes the contract; the fix belongs on the frontend site, mirroring the guard in `comment-ops.ts#applySetResolved`.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:141-144 — `} else { delete t.resolvedAt; delete t.resolvedBy; }` with no `!== undefined` guard, unlike the new backend `applySetResolved`.

samples.summary: `addSlide` feeds `readSlidesRoot`'s output into `MemSlidesStore`, and `readSlidesRoot` returns `themes: []` / `masters: []` for a deck whose root has not been materialized. `MemSlidesStore.addSlide` seeds placeholder text styling only when both a master and a theme resolve, so on such a deck an API-added slide gets placeholders with no master-derived fontSize/fontFamily/color — unlike the same slide added in the editor, which runs after `ensureSlidesRoot` has backfilled `themes`/`masters`. Narrow window (a deck created but never opened), and the constructor's `migrateDocument` substitutes defaults on `read()`, which is why I am not certain the seeding gap is reachable end-to-end.
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:181-213 — `const master = this.doc.masters.find(...) ?? this.doc.masters[0]` then `if (cloned.type === 'text' && master && theme)`; with `masters: []`/`themes: []` from packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:64-65 both are undefined and the seeding branch is skipped. The editor's lazy backfill is packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:252-257.

samples.summary: `duplicateTab` copies only `kind`, `datasourceId` and `query` off the source `TabMeta`, dropping `lakehouseSourceId`, `lakehouseRef` and `asOf`. Unreachable today — the controller refuses a tab with no `sheets` entry, and lakehouse/datasource tabs have none — but the copy is written against a five-field-narrower view of a type that has nine, so the moment an external tab type gains a worksheet the duplicate silently produces a lakehouse tab with no table reference, which `lakehouse-view.tsx` reads directly.

The sheet `createThread` arm lazily creates the thread map (`if (!ws.comments) ws.comments = {}`), which is the exact pattern two places in the repo document as the LWW hazard the eagerly-seeded map exists to avoid: two writers creating the first comment concurrently each assign a fresh map and one thread is dropped wholesale. In practice `createWorksheet` seeds `comments: {}` and the write passes `initialSpreadsheetDocument()` as `initialRoot`, so the key is almost always present — and the editor's own `ensureComments` does the same thing — hence minor rather than a data-loss finding.
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:158-165 states the rule ("If the map were instead created lazily on first comment … one — with its thread — would be dropped wholesale"); restated at packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:547-553. The editor's matching lazy create is packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:3-6.

finding.summary: `unwrapJson`'s new `catch { detachYorkieValue(value) }` fallback silently changes behaviour for its four pre-existing callers, three of which document that `detachYorkieValue` returns WRONG data for their shapes
finding.evidence:
The diff changes `unwrapJson` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:21-25) from `JSON.parse(str)` (throws on failure) to `parseJsonSnapshot(str)` with a fallback to `detachYorkieValue(value)`. Out-of-diff consumers that never asked for that fallback:
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:62-71 — its own comment states: "`unwrapJson`, never a spread and never `detachYorkieValue` … `detachYorkieValue` does not save it either — it branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for an array proxy, so the array comes back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata." With the new fallback, a chart whose repaired parse still fails is now returned to the caller as chart metadata garbage (`seriesColumns: {createdAt, movedAt}`) with HTTP 200, instead of the previous loud 500.
- packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:69-75 and 117-121 make the identical argument ("`unwrapJson`, not `detachYorkieValue`") and are now silently downgraded the same way.
- packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:64-68 unwraps `themes/masters/layouts/slides/guides` array proxies — exactly the `Array.isArray`-false case — so a parse failure now yields CRDT-metadata objects where a deck was expected, which then flows into `readSlidesRoot` consumers including the new `slide-ops` writers.
The fallback is only needed by the new `tabs.duplicate` path; scoping it there (or to a separate helper) would leave the existing readers' documented contract intact.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that `unwrapJson` now wraps its parse in `try { parseJsonSnapshot(str) } catch { detachYorkieValue(value) }` — is not in this repository. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:22-34` is the sole definition of `unwrapJson` (grep for `function unwrapJson|unwrapJson =` returns exactly one hit repo-wide), and it contains no try/catch and no reference to `detachYorkieValue`; `parseJsonSnapshot(str)` is called bare, so an unrepairable snapshot still throws. The helper's doc comment at yorkie-json.ts:13-20 explicitly documents that throw-rather-than-detach contract, and a live test at yorkie-json.spec.ts:155-162 asserts `expect(() => unwrapJson(proxy)).toThrow(SyntaxError)` for exactly the "repaired parse still fails" case — which would fail if the described fallback existed. A repo-wide grep shows `detachYorkieValue` is only used at yorkie-json.ts:153/173/182 (definition + recursion), yorkie-json.ts:217 (inside the separate `snapshotJsonRoot` third tier), comment-ops.ts:99, and a private copy in scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:121 — none reachable from `unwrapJson`. Since the interface change does not exist, the cited consumers (worksheet-charts.controller.ts:58-76, worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:69-75 and 117-121, slides-tree.ts:64-68) keep the loud-failure behaviour their comments describe, and there is no silent downgrade to CRDT-metadata garbage. Ground: not-present.
